what_its_for: Tedizolid is an antibiotic used to treat a type of serious skin infection called acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI). These infections may be caused by certain bacteria, including MRSA (methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus). It works by stopping bacteria from growing and multiplying.
how_to_take: Tedizolid comes as a tablet you swallow by mouth or as an injection given by a healthcare provider into your vein (IV). The tablet can be taken with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush or chew the tablet. If you are receiving the IV form, it will be given to you in a clinic or hospital by a nurse or doctor. Take this medicine at the same time each day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual dose for adults is 200 mg (one tablet) once a day for 6 days. Your doctor will decide the right dose and length of treatment for you. Do not take more or less than your doctor prescribed, and do not stop taking it early even if you feel better. Finishing the full course of antibiotics is very important to make sure the infection is fully treated.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular scheduled time. Do not take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed dose. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store the tablets at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep them away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep this medicine in its original container and out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the package. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused tablets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking tedizolid if you are also taking certain medicines that affect a chemical in your body called serotonin, such as some antidepressants (SSRIs, SNRIs, MAOIs, tricyclics), migraine medicines (triptans), or certain pain medicines like tramadol or meperidine, as this could lead to a serious condition called serotonin syndrome. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist about all medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting tedizolid. Avoid skipping doses or stopping your medicine early, as this can allow bacteria to become resistant to treatment. If you experience diarrhea, avoid using anti-diarrhea medicine without first checking with your doctor.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: signs of serotonin syndrome such as agitation, confusion, fast heartbeat, heavy sweating, muscle twitching or stiffness, or loss of coordination; severe diarrhea that is watery or bloody, which could be a sign of a serious gut infection (C. difficile); vision changes or eye problems such as blurred vision or trouble seeing colors; signs of low blood cell counts such as unusual tiredness, pale skin, easy bruising or bleeding, or frequent infections; severe allergic reaction symptoms such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also contact your doctor if your skin infection does not seem to be getting better or is getting worse.
when_it_works: Most patients start to feel improvement within 2 to 3 days of starting treatment. However, it is very important to finish all 6 days of your prescription even if you feel better sooner. Stopping early can allow the infection to come back or make it harder to treat. If you do not notice any improvement after 2 to 3 days, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. It is not fully known if tedizolid is safe during pregnancy or if it passes into breast milk. Your doctor will weigh the risks and benefits for you. Children: Tedizolid is approved for use in children 12 years and older at the same dose as adults. It has not been studied in children under 12 years old. Older Adults: No dose adjustment is needed for older adults. Kidney or Liver Problems: No dose adjustment is needed for patients with kidney or liver problems, but always tell your doctor about any medical conditions you have before starting this medicine.
